title: Approach of Sages and Hermits
introduction: After the heavenward journey of Sage Sharabhanga, Rama is approached by others sages and hermits. They inform him about the atrocities of demons around that place. They all ask Rama to eradicate the menace and Rama avows to do so, in order to keep up the tranquillity of those hermitages, and also to obliterate the menace of demons from earth.
closing: We have not heard of any chariot or horse being utilised by Rama, let alone in some episodes of his student days, because he is more a foot soldier than a horse/chariot rider. How these sages suddenly say that Rama is a speedy charioteer, is the question. This mahā rathaḥ concept is on the analogy of Krishna the charioteer in Bharata. In Vedanta, the human body is frequently referred as ratha, as in aśva krānte rathaḥ krānte viśṇukrānte vasuṃdharā... , Sec. I-37 Mahanaaraayano panishad: 'O, earth that is traversed by a horse [in Vedic rituals,] a chariot, [great souls, why they all when] Vishnu himself treaded on you as Trivikrama... hence I pray you...' Hence the chariot, drawn by the five-senses as its horses, and the earth are also brought and said here by sages. Krishna-Arjuna's chariot too had five-horses. Here the sages with controlled senses, namely horses, are asking the one who chariots/spins the earth and earthlings, to take off the children of lesser gods, namely demons, far away from humans where humans are god controlled species.

Though born in Ikshvaku dynasty you are the Supreme Charioteer, hence you are the same Supreme Charioteer of this Earth and earthlings too, as with Indra who protects divinities, you are our protector.
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 6h chapter in Aranya of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
शरभङ्गे दिवम् प्राप्ते मुनि संघाः समागताः |
अभ्यगच्छन्त काकुत्स्थम् रामम् ज्वलित तेजसम्
verses.iast:
śarabhañge divam prāpte muni saṅghāḥ samāgatāḥ |
abhyagacchanta kākutstham rāmam jvalita tejasam
verses.translation: On Sage Sharabhanga attaining heaven, groups of sages assembled and approached Rama of Kakutstha dynasty, who is glowing with resplendence.

verses.devanagari:
वैखानसा वालखिल्याः संप्रक्षाला मरीचिपाः |
अश्म कुट्टाः च बहवः पत्र आहाराः च तापसाः
verses.iast:
vaikhānasā vālakhilyāḥ samprakṣālā marīcipāḥ |
aśma kuṭṭāḥ ca bahavaḥ patra āhārāḥ ca tāpasāḥ
verses.translation: The sages called Vaikahanasa-s, [who are born out of the nails of Prajaapati, the first ruler of mankind,] also Vaalakhilyaa-s, [those born from His hair,] and those from the water of His feet-wash, and those that thrive on drinking rays of sun and moon alone, and those that pound with stones and others who thrive on leaves alone, are those sages...
notes: The samprakśāla are kind of sages said be washing their interior body with water, a yogic measure called dhouli prakriya , and also otherwise attributed to wash their vessels after a meal, without preserving any food for the next meal, for god would automatically give their daily bread. The sages called aśma kuṭṭa, are that kind of sages who pound their bodies with stones, and thus they pound grain with stones.

glosses.meaning: sages born out of the nails of Prajaapati
rays of sun and moon, drinkers

verses.devanagari:
दन्त उलूखलिनः च एव तथा एव उन्मज्जकाः परे |
गात्र शय्या अशय्याः च तथा एव अनवकाशिकाः
verses.iast:
danta ulūkhalinaḥ ca eva tathā eva un.hmajjakāḥ pare |
gātra śayyā aśayyāḥ ca tathā eva anavakāśikāḥ
verses.translation: Some of them use their own teeth to grid the grain they eat, and some who perform ascesis in neck-deep water, and some who sleep with their head resting on their shoulders or on chests without using any kind of bed, and some who do not use any kind of beds either, and some who meditate without any repose sitting in an enclosure without any leg-space.

glosses.meaning: teeth, grind-stones, like [use their own teeth to grind the grain]
neck deep in water [they perform ascesis]
sleeper on their own shoulders or chest

verses.devanagari:
मुनयः सलिल आहारा वायु भक्षाः तथा अपरे |
आकाश निलयाः च एव तथा स्थण्डिल शायिनः
verses.iast:
munayaḥ salila āhārā vāyu bhakṣāḥ tathā apare |
ākāśa nilayāḥ ca eva tathā sthaṇḍila śāyinaḥ
verses.translation: And some sages whose food is water alone, or air alone to some, like that some who meditate staying in sky and some who sleep on bare ground itself.

verses.devanagari:
तथा ऊर्थ्व वासिनः दान्ताः तथा आर्द्र पट वाससः |
स जपाः च तपो नित्याः तथा पंच तपोऽन्विताः
verses.iast:
tathā ūrthva vāsinaḥ dāntāḥ tathā ārdra paṭa vāsasaḥ |
sa japāḥ ca tapo nityāḥ tathā pañca tapo'nvitāḥ
verses.translation: Thus some are dwellers on high-peaked places with their senses controlled, and some are wearers of wet cloths, always reciting name or hymn japa and like that some who meditate with five kinds of fire around them.

glosses.meaning: in five kinds of fire, meditating.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वे ब्राह्ंया श्रिया ज्युक्ता दृढ योग समाहिताः |
शरभंग आश्रमे रामम् अभिजग्मुः च तापसाः
verses.iast:
sarve brāhṃyā śriyā jyuk{}tā dṛḍha yoga samāhitāḥ |
śarabhaṅga āśrame rāmam abhijagmuḥ ca tāpasāḥ
verses.translation: All have Vedic resplendence and firm yogic control, and they have arrived at the hermitage of Sage Sharabhanga for Rama.

verses.devanagari:
अभिगंय च धर्मज्ञा रामम् धर्म भृताम् वरम् |
ऊचुः परम धर्मज्ञम् ऋषि संघाः समागताः
verses.iast:
abhigaṃya ca dharmaGYā rāmam dharma bhṛtām varam |
ūcuḥ parama dharmaGYam ṛṣi saṅghāḥ samāgatāḥ
verses.translation: Those virtuous sages coming together in groups neared Rama, the best beholder of virtue, and said to that supreme one in virtue.
notes: The word abhi gamya is nearly approaching, coming nearby, at a destination that is Rama. The Omni-Luminescent, , emerged in Kakutstha dynasty as Rama. Knowing that, all the sages of higher knowledge have arrived at their 'destination' in this mortal world itself... Maheshvara Tirtha.

glosses.meaning: virtue beholder, the best, at Rama [also dharma = bow

verses.devanagari:
त्वम् इक्ष्वाकु कुलस्य अस्य पृथिव्याः च महारथः |
प्रधानः च अपि नाथः च देवानाम् मघवान् इव
verses.iast:
tvam ikṣvāku kulasya asya pṛthivyāḥ ca mahārathaḥ |
pradhānaḥ ca api nāthaḥ ca devānām maghavān iva
verses.translation: "You are the supreme charioteer born in Ikshvaku dynasty hence you are the protector of earth under your control. As with Indra, the ruler of divinities you are a similar ruler for us.

glosses.meaning: being great charioteer in battlefields / Supreme Charioteer of Universe
you are, Ikshvaku, dynasty, [not only] the protector

verses.devanagari:
विश्रुतः त्रिषु लोकेषु यशसा विक्रमेण च |
पितृ व्रतत्वम् सत्यम् च त्वयि धर्मः च पुष्कलः
verses.iast:
viśrutaḥ triṣu lokeṣu yaśasā vikrameṇa ca |
pitṛ vratatvam satyam ca tvayi dharmaḥ ca puṣkalaḥ
verses.translation: "You are well renowned in all the three worlds by your repute and valour, and in you abounding are the virtues like truthfulness and devotion to your father, and even righteousness too, is there.
notes: The above is the apparent meaning. The subtext is "Are you, the supreme charioteer of Ikshvaku dynasty alone, like Indra for celestial beings? And are you the supreme charioteer of this earth and earthlings alone? Not so...you are the Supreme of the whole Universe, therefore your reputation is well known in all the three worlds. Thus you the Omni-Luminescent entered in Ikshvaku dynasty in the form of Rama, to perform your duties like abiding by father's word, with your usual qualities like abounding virtuousness, safeguarding dharma in respect of your own creation/ maintenance..." Thus this is the confrontation-like- addressing of the enlightened sages. Maheshvara Tirtha.

glosses.itrans: triSu lokeshu yashasaa vikrameNa ca vishrutaH
glosses.iast: triṣu lokeśu yaśasā vikrameṇa ca viśrutaḥ
glosses.devanagari: त्रिषु लोकेशु यशसा विक्रमेण च विश्रुतः
glosses.meaning: in three, worlds, by your repute and valour well, renowned

verses.devanagari:
त्वाम् आसाद्य महात्मानम् धर्मज्ञम् धर्म वत्सलम् |
अर्थित्वात् नाथ वक्ष्यामः तत् च नः क्षन्तुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
tvām āsādya mahātmānam dharmaGYam dharma vatsalam |
arthitvāt nātha vakṣyāmaḥ tat ca naḥ kṣantum arhasi
verses.translation: "You are the great-souled one, knower of righteousness and a patron of virtue... such as you are, on approaching you we beg to state something for which we may please be excused...
notes: Special supplication to god is a waste. His mercy has to flows on its own accord. Why beg him to perform his own duty? If by mistake, an appeal is made to god to alleviate a personal problem, his pardon may to be begged, but he is not be begged to do favours. Here the sages on one hand say that 'you have come here in the incarnation of Rama to eradicate evil...' At the same time, they say 'we have an appeal for the same...' This begging off, is as per social custom, made to the apparent ruler of the kingdom, not to the innate Divine.

glosses.meaning: you, like begging, on getting at [we beg to state as we have come across you]
we can tell you [petition to you]
to pardon, will be apt of you.

verses.devanagari:
अधार्मः सुमहान् नाथ भवेत् तस्य तु भूपतेः |
यो हरेत् बलि षड् भागम् न च रक्षति पुत्रवत्
verses.iast:
adhārmaḥ sumahān nātha bhavet tasya tu bhūpateḥ |
yo haret bali ṣaḍ bhāgam na ca rakṣati putravat
verses.translation: "Oh! , very great a-dharma, wrongness, will occur to that king who takes the sixth part of the country's produce as cess, but does not safeguard his subjects like his own sons...
notes: "Protection of subjects is but natural to all kings, but some kings do so for a particular reason, hence this appeal of ours" thus say the sages...Govindaraja. "Though you incarnated yourself to protect the entire universe, so you have to protect us too...but why a special appeal of ours when you are duty bound... that means, we with an unbearable angst of ours make this appeal according to the social custom, but not to harass you. Hence we remind you, Rama, of your kingly duties to safeguard us..." Maheshvara Tirtha. atra a pramaadena prajaaH samrakShaNiiyaaH - rakShaNaat uttama loka avaaptiH - arakShaNe doShaH ca bhavati iti suucitam - dharmaakuutam

verses.devanagari:
युंजानः स्वान् इव प्राणान् प्राणैः इष्टान् सुतान् इव |
नित्य युक्तः सदा रक्षन् सर्वान् विषय वासिनः
प्राप्नोति शाश्वतीम् राम कीर्तिम् स बहु वार्षिकीम् |
ब्रह्मणः स्थानम् आसाद्य तत्र च अपि महीयते
verses.iast:
yuñjānaḥ svān iva prāṇān prāṇaiḥ iṣṭān sutān iva |
nitya yuk{}taḥ sadā rakṣan sarvān viṣaya vāsinaḥ
prāpnoti śāśvatīm rāma kīrtim sa bahu vārṣikīm |
brahmaṇaḥ sthānam āsādya tatra ca api mahīyate
verses.translation: "A king shall treat all the subjects of kingdom as his own sons, and he shall protect them as though he is ready to save them at the cost of his own lives, and he who will always be endeavouring in that manner will attain permanent renown lasting for many for many years to come, and thereby he attains a prosperous place even in Brahma's abode...

glosses.meaning: his own, lives, give away, as though
in Brahma's abode, a place, on getting

verses.devanagari:
यत् करोति परम् धर्मम् मुनिः मूल फल अशनः |
तत्र राज्ञः चतुर् भागः प्रजा धर्मेण रक्षतः
verses.iast:
yat karoti param dharmam muniḥ mūla phala aśanaḥ |
tatra rāGYaḥ catur bhāgaḥ prajā dharmeṇa rakṣataḥ
verses.translation: "He who righteously protects his subjects will get one fourth of the merit of great duty-bound deeds performed by each individual sage, say yajna-s, ascesis, meditation etc. performances.

glosses.meaning: there [from sage,] to that king, fourth, part

verses.devanagari:
सो अयम् ब्राह्मण भूयिष्ठो वानप्रस्थ गणो महान् |
त्वम् नाथो अनाथवत् राम राक्षसैः हन्यते भृशम्
verses.iast:
so ayam brāhmaṇa bhūyiṣṭho vānaprastha gaṇo mahān |
tvam nātho anāthavat rāma rākṣasaiḥ hanyate bhṛśam
verses.translation: "O, Rama, though you are there as protector for the hermitages, suchlike this one, where the most reverent Brahmans are there numerously, they look as though forsaken, for they are being demolished by demons, devastatingly...

glosses.meaning: while you are, there as protector

verses.devanagari:
एहि पश्य शरीराणि मुनीनाम् भावित आत्मनाम् |
हतानाम् राक्षसैः घोरैः बहूनाम् बहुधा वने
verses.iast:
ehi paśya śarīrāṇi munīnām bhāvita ātmanām |
hatānām rākṣasaiḥ ghoraiḥ bahūnām bahudhā vane
verses.translation: "Come and see many of the bodies of the sages, the contemplative souls, that are variously killed by ghastly demons in the forest...

glosses.meaning: in forest, by ghastly, demons, variously, killed

verses.devanagari:
पंपा नदी निवासानाम् अनुमन्दाकिनीम् अपि |
चित्रकूट आलयानाम् च क्रियते कदनम् महत्
verses.iast:
pampā nadī nivāsānām anumandākinīm api |
citrakūṭa ālayānām ca kriyate kadanam mahat
verses.translation: "At Pampa riverside, and alongside of River Mandakini, and at the surroundings of Mt. Chitrakuta also, this hideous warfare is being done...

verses.devanagari:
एवम् वयम् न मृष्यामो विप्रकारम् तपस्विनाम् |
क्रियमाणम् वने घोरम् रक्षोभिः भीम कर्मभिः
verses.iast:
evam vayam na mṛṣyāmo viprakāram tapasvinām |
kriyamāṇam vane ghoram rakṣobhiḥ bhīma karmabhiḥ
verses.translation: "Thus. we are not able to tolerate this injustice to the sages, being executed in this forest by the demons with fiendish deeds, in a ghastly manner...

glosses.meaning: thus, we, not able to tolerate
being executed by, in forest, in a ghastly manner

verses.devanagari:
ततः त्वाम् शरणार्थम् च शरण्यम् समुपस्थिताः |
परिपालय नः राम वध्यमानान् निशाचरैः
verses.iast:
tataḥ tvām śaraṇārtham ca śaraṇyam samupasthitāḥ |
paripālaya naḥ rāma vadhyamānān niśācaraiḥ
verses.translation: "Therefore we present ourselves before you as you are our protector, for the purpose of your protecting us that are being killed by nightwalkers... please safe guard us...
notes: It is said as 'you are the only refuge' because there is no pre or post verbs for this śaraṇyam, thus you aare the protector of all worlds. śaraṇa artham is taken as to 'place us at our appropriate place,' namely in the abode after total salvation; sam upasthitā or sam upāgamā as in other versions, we have come here with viśvāsa, faithfulness, śaraṇāgati , servitude, kainkarya , surrender etc.; naḥ paripālaya protect us and with this word, it is again repeated in next verse as paripālaya naḥ ; and later in the verse the request - from what to be protected is said. That is aniṣṭa nivṛtti rūpa phala prārthana, 'removal of that which is undesirable.' That is to say: 'we better be given total salvation rather than killed by these demons, which is half way through our exercise to attain total salvation.' is the subtext of the speech of sages.

glosses.meaning: a protecting one, a you, for protection, for the purpose of

verses.devanagari:
परा त्वत्तः गतिः वीर पृधिव्यम् न उपपद्यते |
परिपालय नः सर्वान् राक्षसेभ्यो नृपात्मजः
verses.iast:
parā tvattaḥ gatiḥ vīra pṛdhivyam na upapadyate |
paripālaya naḥ sarvān rāxasebhyo nṛpātmajaḥ
verses.translation: "Other than you, oh, valorous Rama, no way-out is deducible on this earth, hence oh, prince, protect all of us from the demons...
notes: There is no way-out on this earth, for that matter of fact in all the universe, when the 'earth' becomes upa lakśṇa for all worlds. This is in consonance with the scripture's saying, na anyaḥ panthā vidyate ayanāya...puruṣa sūkta R.V. X-90 and thus those sages say 'we are contaminated with limited fruition of our practices parimita phalatva, and other suchlike limitations. But you are evident here...before our naked eyes...so protect us from the demons...' where the demons, rākśsebhyaḥ comes to mean sarva aniṣṭāḥ, all earthly undesirables. Again coupled with the vocation of 'Oh Prince...' it is said as: "you have come here like a prince of Ayodhya, unlike a wild boar, or a fish or a man-lion, your earlier incarnations, so remember us and give us salvation...

verses.devanagari:
एतत् श्रुत्वा तु काकुत्स्थः तापसानाम् तपस्विनाम् |
इदम् प्रोवाच धर्मात्मा सर्वान् एव तपस्विनः
verses.iast:
etat śrutvā tu kākutsthaḥ tāpasānām tapasvinām |
idam provāca dharmātmā sarvān eva tapasvinaḥ
verses.translation: On hearing all that is said by the sages of great penance, he that virtue souled Rama said this unto all of the sages.

verses.devanagari:
न एवम् अर्हथ माम् वक्तुम् आज्ञाप्यः अहम् तपस्विनाम् |
केवलेन स्व कार्येण प्रवेष्टव्यम् वनम् मया
verses.iast:
na evam arhatha mām vak{}tum āGYāpyaḥ aham tapasvinām |
kevalena sva kāryeṇa praveṣṭavyam vanam mayā
verses.translation: "Unapt is this way of speaking to me...command me, for I am at your behest... just for my personal purpose I had to enter the forests....

glosses.meaning: this way, to me, to speak, not, apt of you

glosses.itrans: kevalena aatma kaaryeNa mayaa vanam praveSTavyam
glosses.iast: kevalena ātma kāryeṇa mayā vanam praveṣṭavyam
glosses.devanagari: केवलेन आत्म कार्येण मया वनं प्रवेष्टव्यं
glosses.meaning: just for, personal purpose, by me, forest had to be entered.

verses.devanagari:
विप्रकारम् अपाक्रष्टुम् राक्षसैः भवताम् इमम् |
पितुः तु निर्देशकरः प्रविष्टो अहम् इदम् वनम्
verses.iast:
viprakāram apākraṣṭum rāxasaiḥ bhavatām imam |
pituḥ tu nirdeśakaraḥ praviṣṭo aham idam vanam
verses.translation: "I entered this forest as ordered by my father and even to obliterate the unconscionable state of yours owing to the misdeeds of demons.
notes: Rama's saying that 'I am at your command, oh sages...' is indicative of his nature of bhakta jana vaśya... in the control of his ardent devotees, so no special prayer for salvation is needed. In the expression kevalene ātma/sva kāryeṇa... the word kevala is not a kevala pada ... just a word... it indicates a radical sense, like 'for that purpose only' meaning to eradicate demonic menace only, I entered the forest...' Because the śeṣin has to come to the rescue of śeṣi, the servant. So 'safeguarding my own servants is my own responsibility and also pleasure, that is why I entered the forests, where my father's orders are nimitta, a concomitant factor, and not that I entered these forest due to my karma, or misfortune...' Govindaraja. According to Maheshvara Tirtha 'My coming to forests at the orders of my father is a fact but concomitant factor in this forest trek is your request to eliminate the demons, which I will do...' This is evident meaning. The latent one is "I have entered these forests only at my own desire to eradicate demons, for they are doing wrong to you, my servants śeṣin-s, and I abide by you, my devotees...' c.f.,

Griffit's Translit: I wait the hests of all of you. / I by mine own occasion led / This mighty forest needs must tread, / And while I keep my sire's decree / Your lives from threatening foes will free.

verses.devanagari:
भवताम् अर्थ सिद्ध्यर्थम् आगतोऽहम् यदृच्छया |
तस्य मे अयम् वने वासो भविष्यति महाफलः |
verses.iast:
bhavatām artha siddhyartham āgato'ham yadṛcchayā |
tasya me ayam vane vāso bhaviṣyati mahāphalaḥ |
verses.translation: "Perchance I have come for the achievement of your purpose, such as I am, dwelling in this forest will immensely be fruitful to me...

glosses.meaning: such as I am, for me

verses.devanagari:
तपस्विनाम् रणे शत्रून् हन्तुम् इच्छामि राक्षसान् |
पश्यन्तु वीर्यम् ऋषयः सः ब्रातुर् मे तपोधनाः
verses.iast:
tapasvinām raṇe śatrūn hantum icchāmi rākṣasān |
paśyantu vīryam ṛṣayaḥ saḥ brātur me tapodhanāḥ
verses.translation: "I wish to eliminate demons, the enemies of sages, in war... let the sages behold my valour, and my brother's valour in doing so..." Thus Rama promised the sages.

glosses.itrans: tapasvinaam shatruun raakshasaan raNe hantum icChaami
glosses.iast: tapasvinām śatrūn rākśasān raṇe hantum icchāmi
glosses.devanagari: तपस्विनां शत्रून् राक्शसान् रणे हन्तुं इच्छामि
glosses.meaning: of sages, enemies, demons, in war, to eliminate, I wish to

verses.devanagari:
दत्त्वा अभयम् च अपि तपो धनानाम्
धर्मे धृइत आत्मा सह लक्ष्मणेन |
तपो धनैः च अपि सह आर्य दत्तः
सुतीक्ष्णम् एव अभिजगाम वीरः
verses.iast:
dattvā abhayam ca api tapo dhanānām
dharme dhṛita ātmā saha lakṣmaṇena |
tapo dhanaiḥ ca api saha ārya dattaḥ
sutīxṇam eva abhijagāma vīraḥ
verses.translation: Thus giving his aegis to the sages, that valiant Rama who is firmly virtue-souled, journeyed towards Sage Suteekshna with Lakshmana and the sages, and along with the one given by Honourable Janaka, namely Seetha.

glosses.meaning: in virtue, one who is firm, soulfully
by Arya, given [by honourable Janaka given - Seetha]
to Sage Suteekshna alone, journeyed forward.
